name: Tessera Adaptive Platform TAP-5 'Chameleon'
description:
The TAP-5 Chameleon is Tessera's modular assault platform, designed to reconfigure between three operational modes without tools. The weapon's core receiver accepts barrel, stock, and feed assemblies that snap-lock into position, allowing an operator to convert from a compact 5.56mm carbine to a 7.62mm battle rifle to a 4.6mm high-velocity PDW configuration in under thirty seconds.

Each configuration carries its own ballistic profile in the weapon's onboard computer, and the BCI smart-link automatically adjusts aim-assist parameters when the operator swaps modules. Tessera sells the TAP-5 as a system — the base receiver plus three conversion kits runs Φ12,000, but the logistics savings of carrying one weapon platform instead of three justify the cost for extended operations.

The Chameleon's weakness is the mechanical complexity of its quick-change system. Each locking interface is a potential failure point, and field conditions can foul the snap-lock mechanisms. Operators who trust the TAP-5 maintain it religiously. Those who don't carry a backup.
specifications: caliber: 5.56mm / 7.62mm / 4.6mm (configurable) effective_range: 350-600m (configuration dependent) rate_of_fire: 650-900 rpm (configuration dependent) magazine_capacity: 20-40 rounds (configuration dependent) weight: 3.1-4.3 kg (configuration dependent)
tactical_use: The TAP-5 provides mission flexibility that no single-caliber platform can match. Operators select their configuration based on expected engagement parameters — 5.56mm for urban patrol, 7.62mm for perimeter defense, 4.6mm for close protection details. The 30-second conversion time means reconfiguration happens during operational pauses rather than requiring return to an armory.
cultural_context: The Chameleon embodies Tessera's design philosophy of adaptive technology. It appeals to operators who pride themselves on versatility and preparation. Critics argue the TAP-5 does three things adequately rather than one thing excellently, and in corporate security circles the debate between Chameleon generalists and dedicated-platform specialists is ongoing and occasionally heated.
story_hooks: A TAP-5 reconfiguration failed during a critical engagement — the snap-lock jammed between modes, leaving the operator with a non-functional weapon at the worst possible moment.
Someone is selling counterfeit TAP-5 conversion kits that look identical to genuine Tessera modules but have subtly different tolerances that cause failures under stress.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, modular assault platform with a distinctly geometric aesthetic. The receiver resembles a precision-engineered aluminum spine with prominent snap-lock hardpoints visible along its length. The weapon has an almost architectural quality — clean lines interrupted by functional interface points that hint at its transformable nature. When configured as a carbine, it reads compact and purposeful; the battle rifle variant stretches into an imposing form factor.
physical_description.dimensions: Carbine config: 82cm overall length, 6.5cm receiver width, 5cm height at charging handle | Battle rifle config: 105cm overall length | PDW config: 68cm overall length. Barrel lengths: 37cm (5.56mm), 42cm (7.62mm), 28cm (4.6mm)
physical_description.weight_description: Carbine feels balanced and controllable despite modular construction — approximately 3.1kg. Battle rifle variant noticeably heftier at 4.3kg, demanding respect from the operator. PDW config lightest at 3.2kg, favoring handling speed over raw mass.
physical_description.primary_material: Aircraft-grade aluminum alloy receiver with hardened steel snap-lock mechanisms. Barrel assemblies feature chrome-lined steel bores. Furniture is reinforced polymer composite with embedded strain-relief channels.
physical_description.finish: Matte anodized aluminum receiver in gunmetal gray with micro-textured surface to reduce reflection. Barrels wear a battle-worn satin chrome finish showing light oxidation at muzzle crowns. Polymer components finished in flat tactical black with subtle crosshatch grip patterns.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray receiver as primary, accented by matte black polymer furniture and satin chrome barrel assemblies. Status LEDs — blue for standby, amber for ballistic profile loaded, red for malfunction — sit recessed in the receiver rail.
physical_description.grip_texture: Ergonomic grip wrapped in soft-touch rubberized polymer with slight waffle texture for purchase even in gloved or augmented hands. Magazine well features pronounced textured ridges for rapid reload indexing. Charging handle wrapped in knurled steel.
distinctive_features: Three prominent snap-lock hardpoints along receiver that catch light distinctly
Recessed status LED array near the ejection port — blue/amber/red indication system
Tessera's modular barcode etched into receiver for BCI pairing
Tensioning knobs at each snap-lock point with fine adjustment grooves
Integrated cable management channels running the receiver length for sling attachment
Witness holes at each locking interface to visually confirm engagement
Muzzle brake threads visible on barrel assemblies — matching interface across all caliber variants
Picatinny rail segments that shift position depending on configuration — appears to flow and reconfigure with the barrel swap
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: TESSERA logo stamped prominently on the receiver rail in sans-serif capitals. TAP-5 designation and caliber marking engraved (not printed) near the magazine well, updated with each configuration swap. Serial number etched in micro-scale beneath the charging handle, difficult to read without magnification. Tier 3+ licensing watermark laser-etched on lower receiver.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained examples show light carbon fouling at snap-lock interfaces and minor wear on witness holes from repeated configuration cycles. Field-worn variants display micro-scratches where technicians have accessed locking mechanisms for cleaning, and faint salt spray corrosion on chrome barrels in extended-operation units. Operators who trust the platform maintain flawless snap-lock surfaces; those who don't often show debris accumulation and hesitant engagement points.
